title: Ecoma Identity deployment topology
description: The declaration from which Cloudflare Worker configurations and preview lifecycle state are derived. It is LOGICAL: it names resources, and carries no Cloudflare-generated identifier and no indirection for obtaining one. Real identifiers exist only in an ephemeral reconciliation descriptor and in generated wrangler configuration, neither of which is tracked.

commented.description: Every block in this manifest carries its own `$comment`. The comments are the reasoning — a ceiling with no stated reason is a number nobody dares change, and a deletion rule with no stated consequence is one nobody dares rely on. `additionalProperties: false` is what keeps a new key from appearing without anyone writing down why.

email.description: The outbound email service for this environment. `service: null` means the environment has none and the renderer omits the binding; `provisioned: false` means a Worker IS named but does not exist, which is a different and louder failure.

service.description: A Worker NAME, not an id. Null only where `mode` is "none".

hosts.description: Hostname per deployable; null for one that serves none. `identity-jobs` is a queue consumer and is null in every environment.

account.description: The one Cloudflare account and the zone it serves. `id` is account context, not a generated resource id: Cloudflare does not mint it and it does not change. It is written here rather than resolved from GitHub so that no workflow, variable or secret can become a second source of truth for it.

naming.description: Name templates. Every name in every environment derives from one of these.

bindings.description: Binding SLOT NAMES per deployable. These are the strings a Worker reads through `env`; they are not Cloudflare resource ids.

cookie_namespaces.description: Complete locale-cookie NAMES per environment. A prefix, not a full name, would leave the name with two owners.

environments.description: Every environment declares the SAME set of keys, including `email`. The development block shipped without one, which nothing caught: the manifest's own comment says the topology checker fails when declarations disagree, and it did not — because there was nothing to disagree with. `email.service` may be null (an environment with no email service); the key itself may not be absent.

grammar.description: Anchored regular expressions matching the whole name. No prefix matching: a `startsWith('identity-pr-')` somewhere in the delete path would eventually match a production name.

never_delete.description: Tested as literal set membership before every delete, in addition to the grammar. The backstop that does not depend on the grammar being correct.
